questions.question: The rectangular point (1, 1) has polar coordinates
questions.explanation: r² = 1² + 1² = 2, so r = √2. tan θ = 1 ÷ 1 = 1, and since x > 0, y > 0 the point is in Quadrant I, so θ = 45°. Answer: (√2, 45°).

questions.question: The rectangular point (0, −6) has polar coordinates
questions.explanation: r² = 0² + (−6)² = 36, so r = 6. The point lies on the negative y-axis, so θ = 270°. Answer: (6, 270°).

questions.question: The rectangular point (5, −12) has polar coordinates (angle to 2 d.p.)
The rectangular point (−5, 5√3) has polar coordinates
Simplify (2 + √(−4))(5 − √(−16)) and write in standard form.
questions.explanation: √(−4) = 2i and √(−16) = 4i, so the product is (2 + 2i)(5 − 4i). Expand: 10 − 8i + 10i − 8i² = 10 + 2i + 8 = 18 + 2i. Answer: 18 + 2i.

questions.question: Simplify (3 − √(−9))(2 + √(−25)) and write in standard form.
questions.explanation: √(−9) = 3i and √(−25) = 5i, so the product is (3 − 3i)(2 + 5i). Expand: 6 + 15i − 6i − 15i² = 6 + 9i + 15 = 21 + 9i. Answer: 21 + 9i.

questions.question: Simplify (1 + √(−4))(1 − √(−4)).
questions.explanation: √(−4) = 2i, so the expression is (1 + 2i)(1 − 2i) = 1² − (2i)² = 1 + 4 = 5. Answer: 5.

questions.question: Simplify (4 − √(−1))(3 + √(−49)) and write in standard form.
questions.explanation: √(−1) = i and √(−49) = 7i, so the product is (4 − i)(3 + 7i). Expand: 12 + 28i − 3i − 7i² = 12 + 25i + 7 = 19 + 25i. Answer: 19 + 25i.

questions.question: i¹⁷ + i¹⁸ + i¹⁹ + i²⁰ =
questions.explanation: The four consecutive powers of i sum to zero: i + i² + i³ + i⁴ = i − 1 − i + 1 = 0. Answer: 0.

questions.question: i⁴⁵ · i⁷ =
questions.explanation: i⁴⁵ = i (since 45 = 4·11 + 1) and i⁷ = i³ = −i (since 7 = 4·1 + 3). Product: i · (−i) = −i² = 1. Answer: 1.

questions.question: The imaginary unit i is defined as
questions.explanation: By definition, i = √(−1), so that i² = −1. Answer: √(−1).

questions.question: The smallest positive integer n for which iⁿ = 1 is
questions.explanation: i¹ = i, i² = −1, i³ = −i, i⁴ = 1. The smallest positive n with iⁿ = 1 is 4. Answer: 4.

questions.question: The imaginary part of the real number 120, when written as a complex number, is
questions.explanation: A real number 120 written as a complex number is 120 + 0i, so its imaginary part is 0. Answer: 0.

questions.question: When faced with the square root of a negative number in an expression, the first thing to do is
options: convert it to a complex number using i
multiply the roots together under one radical
questions.explanation: √(−k) must first be converted to √k · i. Multiplying the roots under one radical (e.g. √(−3)·√(−12) = √36 = 6) gives the wrong sign. Answer: convert it to a complex number using i.

questions.question: The conjugate of a purely imaginary number bi is
questions.explanation: The conjugate of bi = 0 + bi is 0 − bi = −bi. Answer: −bi.

questions.question: If a point has polar coordinates (r, θ) and rectangular coordinates (x, y), then
options: r = x + y and tan θ = x/y
r² = x² + y² and tan θ = y/x
r = x² + y² and tan θ = x/y
r² = x² − y² and tan θ = y/x
questions.explanation: The correct relations are r² = x² + y² and tan θ = y ÷ x, with θ adjusted for quadrant. Answer: r² = x² + y² and tan θ = y/x.

questions.question: Which of the following is a complex number written in standard form?
questions.explanation: Standard form is a + bi with a, b real. Only 4 − 7i is in that form; the others still contain i² or a quotient. Answer: 4 − 7i.
